Introduction\" href=\"#1-introduction\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol is an open standard designed to facilitate communication and interoperability between independent, potentially opaque AI agent systems. In an ecosystem where agents might be built using different frameworks, languages, or by different vendors, A2A provides a common language and interaction model.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThis document provides the detailed technical specification for the A2A protocol. Its primary goal is to enable agents to:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eDiscover each other's capabilities.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eNegotiate interaction modalities (text, files, structured data).\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eManage collaborative tasks.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eSecurely exchange information to achieve user goals \u003cstrong\u003ewithout needing access to each other's internal state, memory, or tools.\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e1.1. Key Goals of A2A\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-11-key-goals-of-a2a\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: 1.1. Key Goals of A2A\" href=\"#11-key-goals-of-a2a\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 gap between disparate agentic systems.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCollaboration:\u003c/strong\u003e Enable agents to delegate tasks, exchange context, and work together on complex user requests.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDiscovery:\u003c/strong\u003e Allow agents to dynamically find and understand the capabilities of other agents.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFlexibility:\u003c/strong\u003e Support various interaction modes including synchronous request/response, streaming for real-time updates, and asynchronous push notifications for long-running tasks.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSecurity:\u003c/strong\u003e Facilitate secure communication patterns suitable for enterprise environments, relying on standard web security practices.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAsynchronicity:\u003c/strong\u003e Natively support long-running tasks and interactions that may involve human-in-the-loop scenarios.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e1.2. standards (HTTP, JSON-RPC 2.0, Server-Sent Events).\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eEnterprise Ready:\u003c/strong\u003e Address authentication, authorization, security, privacy, tracing, and monitoring by aligning with established enterprise practices.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAsync First:\u003c/strong\u003e Designed for (potentially very) long-running tasks and human-in-the-loop interactions.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eModality Agnostic:\u003c/strong\u003e Support exchange of diverse content types including text, audio/video (via file references), structured data/forms, and potentially embedded UI components (e.g., iframes referenced in parts).\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOpaque Execution:\u003c/strong\u003e Agents collaborate based on declared capabilities and exchanged information, without needing to share their internal thoughts, plans, or tool implementations.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eFor a broader understanding of A2A's purpose and benefits, see \u003ca href=\"/a2aproject/A2A/blob/main/docs/topics/what-is-a2a.md\"\u003eWhat is A2A?\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" These are protocol agnostic definitions expressed as Protocol Buffer messages.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLayer 2: Abstract Operations\u003c/strong\u003e describes the Protocol Bindings\u003c/strong\u003e provides concrete mappings of the abstract operations and data structures to specific protocol bindings (JSON-RPC, gRPC, HTTP/REST), including method names, endpoint patterns, and protocol-specific behaviors.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThis layered approach ensures that:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eCore semantics remain consistent across all protocol bindings\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eNew protocol bindings can be added without changing the fundamental data model\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eDevelopers can reason about A2A operations independently of binding concerns\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eInteroperability is maintained through shared understanding of the canonical data model\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" \u003ccode\u003espec/a2a.proto\u003c/code\u003e is the single authoritative normative definition of all protocol data objects and request/response messages. A generated JSON artifact (\u003ccode\u003espec/a2a.json\u003c/code\u003e, produced at build time and not committed) MAY be published for convenience to tooling and the website, but it is a non-normative build artifact. SDK language bindings, schemas, and any other derived forms \u003cstrong\u003eMUST\u003c/strong\u003e be regenerated from the proto (directly or via code generation) rather than edited manually.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eChange Control and Deprecation Lifecycle:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eIntroduction: When a proto message or field is renamed, the new name is added while existing published names remain available, but marked deprecated, until the next major release.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eDocumentation: Migration guidance MUST be provided via an ancillary document when introducing major breaking changes.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAnchors: Legacy documentation anchors MUST be preserved (as hidden HTML anchors) to avoid breaking inbound links.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eSDK/Schema Aliases: SDKs and JSON Schemas SHOULD provide deprecated alias types/definitions to maintain backward compatibility.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eRemoval: A deprecated name SHOULD NOT be removed earlier than the next major version after introduction of its replacement.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAutomated Generation:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe documentation build generates \u003ccode\u003especification/json/a2a.json\u003c/code\u003e on-the-fly (the file is not tracked in source control). Future improvements may publish an OpenAPI v3 + JSON Schema bundle for enhanced tooling.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRationale:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eCentering the proto file as the normative source ensures protocol neutrality, reduces specification drift, and provides a deterministic evolution path for the ecosystem.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e2. For detailed explanations, please refer to the \u003ca href=\"/a2aproject/A2A/blob/main/docs/topics/key-concepts.md\"\u003eKey Concepts guide\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eA2A Client:\u003c/strong\u003e An application or agent that initiates requests to an A2A Server on behalf of a user or another system.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eA2A Server (Remote Agent):\u003c/strong\u003e An agent or agentic system that exposes an A2A-compliant endpoint, processing tasks and providing responses.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAgent Card:\u003c/strong\u003e A JSON metadata document published by an A2A Server, describing its identity, capabilities, skills, service endpoint, and authentication requirements.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eMessage:\u003c/strong\u003e A communication turn between a client and a remote agent, having a \u003ccode\u003erole\u003c/code\u003e (\"user\" or \"agent\") and containing one or more \u003ccode\u003eParts\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTask:\u003c/strong\u003e The fundamental unit of work managed by A2A, identified by a unique ID. Tasks are stateful and progress through a defined lifecycle.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePart:\u003c/strong\u003e The smallest unit of content within a Message or Artifact. Parts can contain text, file references, or structured data.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eArtifact:\u003c/strong\u003e An output (e.g., a document, image, structured data) generated by the agent as a result of a task, composed of \u003ccode\u003eParts\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eStreaming:\u003c/strong\u003e Real-time, incremental updates for tasks (status changes, artifact chunks) delivered via protocol-specific streaming mechanisms.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePush Notifications:\u003c/strong\u003e Asynchronous task updates delivered via server-initiated HTTP POST requests to a client-provided webhook URL, for long-running or disconnected scenarios.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eContext:\u003c/strong\u003e An optional identifier to logically group related tasks and messages.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eExtension:\u003c/strong\u003e A mechanism for agents to provide additional functionality or data beyond the core A2A specification.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e3. The stream MUST follow one of these patterns:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eMessage-only stream:\u003c/strong\u003e If the agent returns a \u003ca href=\"#414-message\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eMessage\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e, the stream MUST contain exactly one \u003ccode\u003eMessage\u003c/code\u003e object and then close immediately. No task tracking or updates are provided.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTask lifecycle stream:\u003c/strong\u003e If the agent returns a \u003ca href=\"#411-task\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eTask\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e, the stream MUST begin with the Task object, followed by zero or more \u003ca href=\"#421-taskstatusupdateevent\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eTaskStatusUpdateEvent\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e or \u003ca href=\"#422-taskartifactupdateevent\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eTaskArtifactUpdateEvent\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e objects. The stream MUST close when the task reaches a terminal state (\u003ccode\u003eTASK_STATE_COMPLETED\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eTASK_STATE_FAILED\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eTASK_STATE_CANCELED\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eTASK_STATE_REJECTED\u003c/code\u003e).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe agent MAY return a \u003ccode\u003eTask\u003c/code\u003e for complex processing with status/artifact updates or MAY return a \u003ccode\u003eMessage\u003c/code\u003e for direct streaming responses without task overhead. This method allows clients to discover and manage multiple tasks across different contexts or with specific status criteria.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eInputs:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e{{ proto_to_table(\"ListTasksRequest\") }}\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eWhen \u003ccode\u003eincludeArtifacts\u003c/code\u003e is false (the default), the artifacts field MUST be omitted entirely from each Task object in the response. The field should not be present as an empty array or null value. When \u003ccode\u003eincludeArtifacts\u003c/code\u003e is true, the artifacts field should be included with its actual content (which may be an empty array if the task has no artifacts).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOutputs:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e{{ proto_to_table(\"ListTasksResponse\") }}\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eNote on \u003ccode\u003enextPageToken\u003c/code\u003e: The \u003ccode\u003enextPageToken\u003c/code\u003e field MUST always be present in the response. When there are no more results to retrieve (i.e., this is the final page), the field MUST be set to an empty string (\"\"). Clients should check for an empty string to determine if more pages are available.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eErrors:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eNone specific to this operation beyond standard protocol errors.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eBehavior:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe operation MUST return only tasks visible to the authenticated client and MUST use cursor-based pagination for performance and consistency. Tasks MUST be sorted by last update time in descending order. Implementations MUST implement appropriate authorization scoping to ensure clients can only access authorized tasks. See \u003ca href=\"#131-data-access-and-authorization-scoping\"\u003eSection 13.1 Data Access and Authorization Scoping\u003c/a\u003e for detailed security requirements.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cem\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePagination Strategy:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThis method uses cursor-based pagination (via \u003ccode\u003epageToken\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003enextPageToken\u003c/code\u003e) rather than offset-based pagination for better performance and consistency, especially with large datasets. Cursor-based pagination avoids the \"deep pagination problem\" where skipping large numbers of records becomes inefficient for databases. This approach is consistent with the gRPC specification, which also uses cursor-based pagination (page_token/next_page_token).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cem\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOrdering:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eImplementations MUST return tasks sorted by their status timestamp time in descending order (most recently updated tasks first). This ensures consistent pagination and allows clients to efficiently monitor recent task activity.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch4 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e3.1.5. Operations are blocking by default:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eBlocking (\u003ccode\u003ereturn_immediately: false\u003c/code\u003e or unset)\u003c/strong\u003e: The operation MUST wait until the task reaches a terminal state (\u003ccode\u003eTASK_STATE_COMPLETED\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eTASK_STATE_FAILED\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eTASK_STATE_CANCELED\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eTASK_STATE_REJECTED\u003c/code\u003e) or an interrupted state (\u003ccode\u003eTASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eTASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED\u003c/code\u003e) before returning. The response MUST include the latest task state with all artifacts and status information. This is the default behavior.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eNon-Blocking (\u003ccode\u003ereturn_immediately: true\u003c/code\u003e)\u003c/strong\u003e: The operation MUST return immediately after creating the task, even if processing is still in progress. The returned task will have an in-progress state (e.g., \u003ccode\u003eTASK_STATE_WORKING\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eTASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED\u003c/code\u003e). It is the caller's responsibility to poll for updates using \u003ca href=\"#313-get-task\"\u003eGet Task\u003c/a\u003e, subscribe via \u003ca href=\"#316-subscribe-to-task\"\u003eSubscribe to Task\u003c/a\u003e, or receive updates via push notifications.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe \u003ccode\u003ereturn_immediately\u003c/code\u003e field has no effect:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003ewhen the operation returns a direct \u003ca href=\"#414-message\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eMessage\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e response instead of a task.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003efor streaming operations, which always return updates in real-time.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eon configured push notification configurations, which operates independently of execution mode.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch4 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e3.2.3. This parameter follows consistent semantics across all operations:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eUnset/undefined\u003c/strong\u003e: No limit imposed; server returns its default amount of history (implementation-defined, may be all history)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e0\u003c/strong\u003e: No history should be returned; the \u003ccode\u003ehistory\u003c/code\u003e field SHOULD be omitted\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u0026gt; 0\u003c/strong\u003e: Return at most this many recent messages from the task's history\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch4 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e3.2.5. Metadata keys and are strings and values can be any valid value that can be represented in JSON. \u003ca href=\"#46-extensions\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eExtensions\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e can be used to strongly type metadata values for specific use cases.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch4 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e3.2.6 Service Parameters\u003c/h4\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-326-service-parameters\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: 3.2.6 Service Parameters\" href=\"#326-service-parameters\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eA key-value map for passing horizontally applicable context or parameters with case-insensitive string keys and case-sensitive string values. The transmission mechanism for these service parameter key-value pairs is defined by the specific protocol binding (e.g., HTTP headers for HTTP-based bindings, gRPC metadata for gRPC bindings). Custom protocol bindings \u003cstrong\u003eMUST\u003c/strong\u003e specify how service parameters are transmitted in their binding specification.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eStandard A2A Service Parameters:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cmarkdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\u003ctable\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003cth align=\"left\"\u003eName\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth align=\"left\"\u003eDescription\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth align=\"left\"\u003eExample Value\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eA2A-Extensions\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003eComma-separated list of extension URIs that the client wants to use for the request\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003ehttps://example.com/extensions/geolocation/v1,https://standards.org/extensions/citations/v1\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eA2A-Version\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003eThe A2A protocol version that the client is using. If the version is not supported, the agent returns \u003ca href=\"#332-error-handling\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eVersionNotSupportedError\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003e0.3\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAs service parameter names MAY need to co-exist with other parameters defined by the underlying transport protocol or infrastructure, all service parameters defined by this specification will be prefixed with \u003ccode\u003ea2a-\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e3.3. Agents may utilize the messageId to detect duplicate messages.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCancel Task\u003c/strong\u003e operations are idempotent - multiple cancellation requests have the same effect. A duplicate cancellation request MAY return \u003ccode\u003eTaskNotFoundError\u003c/code\u003e if the task has already been canceled and purged.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch4 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e3.3.2. Servers \u003cstrong\u003eMUST\u003c/strong\u003e return appropriate errors and \u003cstrong\u003eSHOULD\u003c/strong\u003e provide actionable information to help clients resolve issues.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eError Categories and Server Requirements:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAuthentication Errors\u003c/strong\u003e: Invalid or missing credentials\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eServers \u003cstrong\u003eMUST\u003c/strong\u003e reject requests with invalid or missing authentication credentials\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eServers \u003cstrong\u003eSHOULD\u003c/strong\u003e include authentication challenge information in the error response\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eServers \u003cstrong\u003eSHOULD\u003c/strong\u003e specify which authentication scheme is required\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eExample error codes: HTTP \u003ccode\u003e401 Unauthorized\u003c/code\u003e, gRPC \u003ccode\u003eUNAUTHENTICATED\u003c/code\u003e, JSON-RPC custom error\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eExample scenarios: Missing bearer token, expired API key, invalid OAuth token\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAuthorization Errors\u003c/strong\u003e: Insufficient permissions for requested operation\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eServers \u003cstrong\u003eMUST\u003c/strong\u003e return an authorization error when the authenticated client lacks required permissions\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eServers \u003cstrong\u003eSHOULD\u003c/strong\u003e indicate what permission or scope is missing (without leaking sensitive information about resources the client cannot access)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eServers \u003cstrong\u003eMUST NOT\u003c/strong\u003e reveal the existence of resources the client is not authorized to access\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eExample error codes: HTTP \u003ccode\u003e403 Forbidden\u003c/code\u003e, gRPC \u003ccode\u003ePERMISSION_DENIED\u003c/code\u003e, JSON-RPC custom error\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eExample scenarios: Attempting to access a task created by another user, insufficient OAuth scopes\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eValidation Errors\u003c/strong\u003e: Invalid input parameters or message format\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eServers \u003cstrong\u003eMUST\u003c/strong\u003e validate all input parameters before processing\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eServers \u003cstrong\u003eSHOULD\u003c/strong\u003e specify which parameter(s) failed validation and why\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eServers \u003cstrong\u003eSHOULD\u003c/strong\u003e provide guidance on valid parameter values or formats\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eExample error codes: HTTP \u003ccode\u003e400 Bad Request\u003c/code\u003e, gRPC \u003ccode\u003eINVALID_ARGUMENT\u003c/code\u003e, JSON-RPC \u003ccode\u003e-32602 Invalid params\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eExample scenarios: Invalid task ID format, missing required message parts, unsupported content type\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eResource Errors\u003c/strong\u003e: Requested task not found or not accessible\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eServers \u003cstrong\u003eMUST\u003c/strong\u003e return a not found error when a requested resource does not exist or is not accessible to the authenticated client\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eServers \u003cstrong\u003eSHOULD NOT\u003c/strong\u003e distinguish between \"does not exist\" and \"not authorized\" to prevent information leakage\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eExample error codes: HTTP \u003ccode\u003e404 Not Found\u003c/code\u003e, gRPC \u003ccode\u003eNOT_FOUND\u003c/code\u003e, JSON-RPC custom error (see A2A-specific errors)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eExample scenarios: Task ID does not exist, task has been deleted, configuration not found\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSystem Errors\u003c/strong\u003e: Internal agent failures or temporary unavailability\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eServers \u003cstrong\u003eSHOULD\u003c/strong\u003e return appropriate error codes for temporary failures vs. permanent errors\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eServers \u003cstrong\u003eMAY\u003c/strong\u003e include retry guidance (e.g., Retry-After header in HTTP)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eServers \u003cstrong\u003eSHOULD\u003c/strong\u003e log system errors for diagnostic purposes\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eExample error codes: HTTP \u003ccode\u003e500 Internal Server Error\u003c/code\u003e or \u003ccode\u003e503 Service Unavailable\u003c/code\u003e, gRPC \u003ccode\u003eINTERNAL\u003c/code\u003e or \u003ccode\u003eUNAVAILABLE\u003c/code\u003e, JSON-RPC \u003ccode\u003e-32603 Internal error\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eExample scenarios: Database connection failure, downstream service timeout, rate limit exceeded\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eError Payload Structure:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAll error responses in the A2A protocol, regardless of binding, \u003cstrong\u003eMUST\u003c/strong\u003e convey the following information:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eError Code\u003c/strong\u003e: A machine-readable identifier for the error type (e.g., string code, numeric code, or protocol-specific status)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eError Message\u003c/strong\u003e: A human-readable description of the error\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eError Details\u003c/strong\u003e (optional): An array of objects providing additional structured information about the error. Each object in the array \u003cstrong\u003eMUST\u003c/strong\u003e include a \u003ccode\u003e@type\u003c/code\u003e key that identifies the object's type (using \u003ca href=\"https://protobuf.dev/programming-guides/json\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eProtoJSON \u003ccode\u003eAny\u003c/code\u003e representation\u003c/a\u003e). Well-known types from the \u003ca href=\"https://cloud.google.com/apis/design/errors#error_model\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003egoogle.rpc\u003c/code\u003e error model\u003c/a\u003e (e.g., \u003ccode\u003eErrorInfo\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eBadRequest\u003c/code\u003e) \u003cstrong\u003eSHOULD\u003c/strong\u003e be used where applicable. Error details may be used for:\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAffected fields or parameters\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eContextual information (e.g., task ID, timestamp)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eSuggestions for resolution\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eProtocol bindings \u003cstrong\u003eMUST\u003c/strong\u003e map these elements to their native error representations while preserving semantic meaning. See binding-specific sections for concrete error format examples: \u003ca href=\"#95-error-handling\"\u003eJSON-RPC Error Handling\u003c/a\u003e, \u003ca href=\"#106-error-handling\"\u003egRPC Error Handling\u003c/a\u003e, and \u003ca href=\"#116-error-handling\"\u003eHTTP/REST Error Handling\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eA2A-Specific Errors:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cmarkdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\u003ctable\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003cth align=\"left\"\u003eError Name\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth align=\"left\"\u003eDescription\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eTaskNotFoundError\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003eThe specified task ID does not correspond to an existing or accessible task. It might be invalid, expired, or already completed and purged.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eTaskNotCancelableError\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003eAn attempt was made to cancel a task that is not in a cancelable state (e.g., it has already reached a terminal state like \u003ccode\u003eTASK_STATE_COMPLETED\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eTASK_STATE_FAILED\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eTASK_STATE_CANCELED\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eTASK_STATE_REJECTED\u003c/code\u003e).\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003ePushNotificationNotSupportedError\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003eClient attempted to use push notification features but the server agent does not support them (i.e., \u003ccode\u003eAgentCard.capabilities.pushNotifications\u003c/code\u003e is \u003ccode\u003efalse\u003c/code\u003e).\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eUnsupportedOperationError\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003eThe requested operation or a specific aspect of it is not supported by this server agent implementation.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eContentTypeNotSupportedError\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003eA Media Type provided in the request's message parts or implied for an artifact is not supported by the agent or the specific skill being invoked.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eInvalidAgentResponseError\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003eAn agent returned a response that does not conform to the specification for the current method.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eExtendedAgentCardNotConfiguredError\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003eThe agent does not have an extended agent card configured when one is required for the requested operation.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eExtensionSupportRequiredError\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003eServer requested use of an extension marked as \u003ccode\u003erequired: true\u003c/code\u003e in the Agent Card but the client did not declare support for it in the request.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eVersionNotSupportedError\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd align=\"left\"\u003eThe A2A protocol version specified in the request (via \u003ccode\u003eA2A-Version\u003c/code\u003e service parameter) is not supported by the agent.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch4 tabindex=\"-1\" Asynchronous Processing\" href=\"#333-asynchronous-processing\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eA2A operations are designed for asynchronous task execution. Operations return immediately with either \u003ca href=\"#411-task\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eTask\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e objects or \u003ca href=\"#414-message\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eMessage\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e objects, and when a Task is returned, processing continues in the background. Clients retrieve task updates through polling, streaming, or push notifications (see \u003ca href=\"#35-task-update-delivery-mechanisms\"\u003eSection 3.5\u003c/a\u003e). Agents MAY accept additional messages for tasks in non-terminal states to enable multi-turn interactions (see \u003ca href=\"#34-multi-turn-interactions\"\u003eSection 3.4\u003c/a\u003e).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch4 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e3.3.4. Capability Validation\u003c/h4\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-334-capability-validation\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: 3.3.4. Capability Validation\" href=\"#334-capability-validation\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAgents declare optional capabilities in their \u003ca href=\"#441-agentcard\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eAgentCard\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e. When clients attempt to use operations or features that require capabilities not declared as supported in the Agent Card, the agent \u003cstrong\u003eMUST\u003c/strong\u003e return an appropriate error response:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePush Notifications\u003c/strong\u003e: If \u003ccode\u003eAgentCard.capabilities.pushNotifications\u003c/code\u003e is \u003ccode\u003efalse\u003c/code\u003e or not present, operations related to push notification configuration (Create, Get, List, Delete) \u003cstrong\u003eMUST\u003c/strong\u003e return \u003ca href=\"#332-error-handling\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003ePushNotificationNotSupportedError\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eStreaming\u003c/strong\u003e: If \u003ccode\u003eAgentCard.capabilities.streaming\u003c/code\u003e is \u003ccode\u003efalse\u003c/code\u003e or not present, attempts to use \u003ccode\u003eSendStreamingMessage\u003c/code\u003e or \u003ccode\u003eSubscribeToTask\u003c/code\u003e operations \u003cstrong\u003eMUST\u003c/strong\u003e return \u003ca href=\"#332-error-handling\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eUnsupportedOperationError\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eExtended Agent Card\u003c/strong\u003e: If \u003ccode\u003eAgentCard.capabilities.extendedAgentCard\u003c/code\u003e is \u003ccode\u003efalse\u003c/code\u003e or not present, attempts to call the Get Extended Agent Card operation \u003cstrong\u003eMUST\u003c/strong\u003e return \u003ca href=\"#332-error-handling\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eUnsupportedOperationError\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e. If the agent declares support but has not configured an extended card, it \u003cstrong\u003eMUST\u003c/strong\u003e return \u003ca href=\"#332-error-handling\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eExtendedAgentCardNotConfiguredError\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eExtensions\u003c/strong\u003e: When a server requests use of an extension marked as \u003ccode\u003erequired: true\u003c/code\u003e in the Agent Card but the client does not declare support for it, the agent \u003cstrong\u003eMUST\u003c/strong\u003e return \u003ca href=\"#332-error-handling\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eExtensionSupportRequiredError\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eClients \u003cstrong\u003eSHOULD\u003c/strong\u003e validate capability support by examining the Agent Card before attempting operations that require optional capabilities.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e3.4. Multi-Turn Interactions\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-34-multi-turn-interactions\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: 3.4. related \u003ca href=\"#411-task\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eTask\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e and \u003ca href=\"#414-message\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eMessage\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e objects, providing continuity across a series of interactions.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eGeneration and Assignment:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAgents \u003cstrong\u003eMAY\u003c/strong\u003e generate a new \u003ccode\u003econtextId\u003c/code\u003e when processing a \u003ca href=\"#414-message\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eMessage\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e that does not include a \u003ccode\u003econtextId\u003c/code\u003e field\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eIf an agent generates a new \u003ccode\u003econtextId\u003c/code\u003e, it \u003cstrong\u003eMUST\u003c/strong\u003e be included in the response (either \u003ca href=\"#411-task\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eTask\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e or \u003ca href=\"#414-message\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eMessage\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAgents \u003cstrong\u003eMAY\u003c/strong\u003e accept and preserve client-provided \u003ccode\u003econtextId\u003c/code\u003e values\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eIf an agent cannot accept a client-provided \u003ccode\u003econtextId\u003c/code\u003e, it \u003cstrong\u003eMUST\u003c/strong\u003e reject the request with an error and \u003cstrong\u003eMUST NOT\u003c/strong\u003e generate a new \u003ccode\u003econtextId\u003c/code\u003e for the response\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eClients \u003cstrong\u003eSHOULD NOT\u003c/strong\u003e provide a client-generated \u003ccode\u003econtextId\u003c/code\u003e to a server unless they understand how the server will process that \u003ccode\u003econtextId\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eServer-generated \u003ccode\u003econtextId\u003c/code\u003e values \u003cstrong\u003eSHOULD\u003c/strong\u003e be treated as opaque identifiers by clients\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eGrouping and Scope:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eA \u003ccode\u003econtextId\u003c/code\u003e logically groups multiple \u003ca href=\"#411-task\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eTask\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e objects and \u003ca href=\"#414-message\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eMessage\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e objects that are part of the same conversational context\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAll tasks and messages with the same \u003ccode\u003econtextId\u003c/code\u003e \u003cstrong\u003eSHOULD\u003c/strong\u003e be treated as part of the same conversational session\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAgents \u003cstrong\u003eMAY\u003c/strong\u003e use the \u003ccode\u003econtextId\u003c/code\u003e to maintain internal state, conversational history, or LLM context across multiple interactions\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAgents \u003cstrong\u003eMAY\u003c/strong\u003e implement context expiration or cleanup policies and \u003cstrong\u003eSHOULD\u003c/strong\u003e document any such policies\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch4 tabindex=\"-1\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eGeneration and Assignment:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eTask IDs are \u003cstrong\u003eserver-generated\u003c/strong\u003e when a new task is created in response to a \u003ca href=\"#414-message\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eMessage\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAgents \u003cstrong\u003eMUST\u003c/strong\u003e generate a unique \u003ccode\u003etaskId\u003c/code\u003e for each new task they create\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eThe generated \u003ccode\u003etaskId\u003c/code\u003e \u003cstrong\u003eMUST\u003c/strong\u003e be included in the \u003ca href=\"#411-task\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eTask\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e object returned to the client\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eWhen a client includes a \u003ccode\u003etaskId\u003c/code\u003e in a \u003ca href=\"#414-message\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eMessage\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e, it \u003cstrong\u003eMUST\u003c/strong\u003e reference an existing task\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAgents \u003cstrong\u003eMUST\u003c/strong\u003e return a \u003ca href=\"#332-error-handling\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eTaskNotFoundError\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e if the provided \u003ccode\u003etaskId\u003c/code\u003e does not correspond to an existing task\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eClient-provided \u003ccode\u003etaskId\u003c/code\u003e values for creating new tasks is \u003cstrong\u003eNOT\u003c/strong\u003e supported\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch4 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e3.4.3. dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eContext Continuity:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"#411-task\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eTask\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e objects maintain conversation context through the \u003ccode\u003econtextId\u003c/code\u003e field\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eClients \u003cstrong\u003eMAY\u003c/strong\u003e include the \u003ccode\u003econtextId\u003c/code\u003e in subsequent messages to indicate continuation of a previous interaction\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eClients \u003cstrong\u003eMAY\u003c/strong\u003e use \u003ccode\u003etaskId\u003c/code\u003e (with or without \u003ccode\u003econtextId\u003c/code\u003e) to continue or refine a specific task\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eClients \u003cstrong\u003eMAY\u003c/strong\u003e use \u003ccode\u003econtextId\u003c/code\u003e without \u003ccode\u003etaskId\u003c/code\u003e to start a new task within an existing conversation context\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAgents \u003cstrong\u003eMUST\u003c/strong\u003e infer \u003ccode\u003econtextId\u003c/code\u003e from the task if only \u003ccode\u003etaskId\u003c/code\u003e is provided\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAgents \u003cstrong\u003eMUST\u003c/strong\u003e reject messages containing mismatching \u003ccode\u003econtextId\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003etaskId\u003c/code\u003e (i.e., the provided \u003ccode\u003econtextId\u003c/code\u003e is different from that of the referenced \u003ca href=\"#411-task\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eTask\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e).\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eInput Required State:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAgents can request additional input mid-processing by transitioning a task to the \u003ccode\u003einput-required\u003c/code\u003e state\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eThe client continues the interaction by sending a new message with the same \u003ccode\u003etaskId\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003econtextId\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFollow-up Messages:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eClients can send additional messages with \u003ccode\u003etaskId\u003c/code\u003e references to continue or refine existing tasks\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eClients \u003cstrong\u003eSHOULD\u003c/strong\u003e use the \u003ccode\u003ereferenceTaskIds\u003c/code\u003e field in \u003ca href=\"#414-message\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eMessage\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e to explicitly reference related tasks\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAgents \u003cstrong\u003eSHOULD\u003c/strong\u003e use referenced tasks to understand the context and intent of follow-up requests\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eContext Inheritance:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eNew tasks created within the same \u003ccode\u003econtextId\u003c/code\u003e can inherit context from previous interactions\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAgents \u003cstrong\u003eSHOULD\u003c/strong\u003e leverage the shared \u003ccode\u003econtextId\u003c/code\u003e to provide contextually relevant responses\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e3.5. updates\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eRequires persistent connection support\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eBest for: Interactive applications, real-time dashboards, live progress monitoring\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eRequires \u003ccode\u003eAgentCard.capabilities.streaming\u003c/code\u003e to be \u003ccode\u003etrue\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePush Notifications (WebHooks):\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAgent sends HTTP POST requests to client-registered endpoints when task state changes\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eClient does not maintain persistent connection\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAsynchronous delivery, client must be reachable via HTTP\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eBest for: Server-to-server integrations, long-running tasks, event-driven architectures\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eOperations: Create (\u003ca href=\"#317-create-push-notification-config\"\u003eSection 3.1.7\u003c/a\u003e), Get (\u003ca href=\"#76-taskspushnotificationconfigget\"\u003eSection 3.1.8\u003c/a\u003e), List (\u003ca href=\"#319-list-push-notification-configs\"\u003eSection 3.1.9\u003c/a\u003e), Delete (\u003ca href=\"#3110-delete-push-notification-config\"\u003eSection 3.1.10\u003c/a\u003e)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eEvent types: TaskStatusUpdateEvent (\u003ca href=\"#421-taskstatusupdateevent\"\u003eSection 4.2.1\u003c/a\u003e), TaskArtifactUpdateEvent (\u003ca href=\"#422-taskartifactupdateevent\"\u003eSection 4.2.2\u003c/a\u003e), WebHook payloads (\u003ca href=\"#43-push-notification-objects\"\u003eSection 4.3\u003c/a\u003e)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eRequires \u003ccode\u003eAgentCard.capabilities.pushNotifications\u003c/code\u003e to be \u003ccode\u003etrue\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eRegardless of the protocol binding being used by the agent, WebHook calls use plain HTTP and the JSON payloads as defined in the HTTP protocol binding\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch4 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e3.5.2. Streaming Event Delivery\u003c/h4\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-352-streaming-event-delivery\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: 3.5.2. Streaming Event Delivery\" href=\"#352-streaming-event-delivery\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eEvent Ordering:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAll implementations MUST deliver events in the order they were generated. Events MUST NOT be reordered during transmission, regardless of protocol binding.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eMultiple Streams Per Task:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAn agent MAY serve multiple concurrent streams to one or more clients for the same task. This allows multiple clients (or the same client with multiple connections) to independently subscribe to and receive updates about a task's progress.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eWhen multiple streams are active for a task:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eEvents MUST be broadcast to all active streams for that task\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eEach stream MUST receive the same events in the same order\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eClosing one stream MUST NOT affect other active streams for the same task\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eThe task lifecycle is independent of any individual stream's lifecycle\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThis capability enables scenarios such as:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eMultiple team members monitoring the same long-running task\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eA client reconnecting to a task after a network interruption by opening a new stream\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eDifferent applications or dashboards displaying real-time updates for the same task\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch4 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e3.5.3. Push Notification Delivery\u003c/h4\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-353-push-notification-delivery\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: 3.5.3. Push Notification Delivery\" href=\"#353-push-notification-delivery\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003ePush notifications are delivered via HTTP POST to client-registered webhook endpoints. The delivery semantics and reliability guarantees are defined in \u003ca href=\"#43-push-notification-objects\"\u003eSection 4.3\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e3.6 Versioning\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-36-versioning\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: 3.6 Versioning\" href=\"#36-versioning\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe specific version of the A2A protocol in use is identified using the \u003ccode\u003eMajor.Minor\u003c/code\u003e elements (e.g. \u003ccode\u003e1.0\u003c/code\u003e) of the corresponding A2A specification version. Patch version numbers used by the specification, do not affect protocol compatibility. Patch version numbers SHOULD NOT be used in requests, responses and Agent Cards, and MUST not be considered when clients and servers negotiate protocol versions.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch4 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e3.6.1 Client Responsibilities\u003c/h4\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-361-client-responsibilities\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: 3.6.1 Client Responsibilities\" href=\"#361-client-responsibilities\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eClients MUST send the \u003ccode\u003eA2A-Version\u003c/code\u003e header with each request to maintain compatibility after an agent upgrades to a new version of the protocol (except for 0.3 Clients - 0.3 will be assumed for empty header). Sending the \u003ccode\u003eA2A-Version\u003c/code\u003e header also provides visibility to agents about version usage in the ecosystem, which can help inform the risks of inplace version upgrades.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eExample of HTTP GET Request with Version Header:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight \u003ccode\u003eA2A-Version\u003c/code\u003e (matching \u003ccode\u003eMajor.Minor\u003c/code\u003e). If the version is not supported by the interface, agents MUST return a \u003ca href=\"#332-error-handling\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eVersionNotSupportedError\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAgents MUST interpret empty value as 0.3 version.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAgents CAN expose multiple interfaces for the same transport with different versions under the same or different URLs.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch4 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e3.6.3 Tooling support\u003c/h4\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-363-tooling-support\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: 3.6.3 Tooling support\" href=\"#363-tooling-support\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eTooling libraries and SDKs that implement the A2A protocol MUST provide mechanisms to help clients manage protocol versioning, such as negotiation of the transport and protocol version used. Client Agents that require the latest features of the protocol should be configured to request specific versions and avoid automatic fallback to older versions, to prevent silently losing functionality.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e3.7 Messages and Artifacts\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-37-messages-and-artifacts\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: 3.7 Messages and Artifacts\" href=\"#37-messages-and-artifacts\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eMessages and Artifacts serve distinct purposes within the A2A protocol. The core interaction model defined by A2A is for clients to send messages to initiate a task that produces one or more artifacts.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eMessages play several key roles:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTask Initiation\u003c/strong\u003e: Clients send Messages to agents to initiate new tasks.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eClarification Messages\u003c/strong\u003e: Agents may send Messages back to the client to request clarification prior to initiating a task.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eStatus Messages\u003c/strong\u003e: Agents attach Messages to status update events to inform clients about task progress, request additional input, or provide informational updates.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTask Interaction\u003c/strong\u003e: Clients send Messages to provide additional input or instructions for ongoing tasks.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eMessages SHOULD NOT be used to deliver task outputs. Results SHOULD BE returned using Artifacts associated with a Task. This separation allows for a clear distinction between communication (Messages) and data output (Artifacts).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe Task History field contains Messages exchanged during task execution. However, not all Messages are guaranteed to be persisted in the Task history; for example, transient informational messages may not be stored. Messages exchanged prior to task creation may not be stored in Task history. The agent is responsible to determine which Messages are persisted in the Task History.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eClients using streaming to retrieve task updates MAY not receive all status update messages if the client is disconnected and then reconnects. Messages MUST NOT be considered a reliable delivery mechanism for critical information.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAgents MAY choose to persist all Messages that contain important information in the Task history to ensure clients can retrieve it later. dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003etask\u003c/strong\u003e: A \u003ca href=\"#411-task\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eTask\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e object with the current task state\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003emessage\u003c/strong\u003e: A \u003ca href=\"#414-message\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eMessage\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e object containing a dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAuthentication:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe agent MUST include authentication credentials in the request headers as specified in the \u003ca href=\"#432-authenticationinfo\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003ePushNotificationConfig.authentication\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e field. The format follows standard HTTP authentication patterns (Bearer tokens, Basic auth, etc.).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eClient Responsibilities:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eClients MUST respond with HTTP 2xx status codes to acknowledge successful receipt\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eClients SHOULD process notifications idempotently, as duplicate deliveries may occur\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eClients MUST validate the task ID matches an expected task\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eClients SHOULD implement appropriate security measures to verify the notification source\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eServer Guarantees:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAgents MUST attempt delivery at least once for each configured webhook\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAgents MAY implement retry logic with exponential backoff for failed deliveries\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAgents SHOULD include a reasonable timeout for webhook requests (recommended: 10-30 seconds)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAgents MAY stop attempting delivery after a configured number of consecutive failures\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eFor detailed security guidance on push notifications, see \u003ca href=\"#132-push-notification-security\"\u003eSection 13.2 Push Notification Security\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e4.4. zero-filled\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eTimestamps \u003cstrong\u003eMUST NOT\u003c/strong\u003e include timezone offsets other than 'Z' (all times are These annotations serve as both documentation and validation hints for implementations.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRequired Fields:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eFields marked with \u003ccode\u003e[(google.api.field_behavior) = REQUIRED]\u003c/code\u003e indicate that the field \u003cstrong\u003eMUST\u003c/strong\u003e be present and set in valid messages. Implementations \u003cstrong\u003eSHOULD\u003c/strong\u003e validate these requirements and reject messages with missing required fields. Arrays marked as required \u003cstrong\u003eMUST\u003c/strong\u003e contain at least one element.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOptional Field Presence:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe Protocol Buffer \u003ccode\u003eoptional\u003c/code\u003e keyword is used to distinguish between a field being explicitly set versus omitted. This distinction is critical for two scenarios:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eExplicit Default Values:\u003c/strong\u003e Some fields in the specification define default values that differ from Protocol Buffer's implicit defaults. Implementations should apply the default value when the field is not explicitly provided.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAgent Card Canonicalization:\u003c/strong\u003e When creating cryptographic signatures of Agent Cards, it is required to produce a canonical JSON representation. The \u003ccode\u003eoptional\u003c/code\u003e keyword enables implementations to distinguish between fields that were explicitly set (and should be included in the canonical form) versus fields that were omitted (and should be excluded from canonicalization). This ensures Agent Cards can be reconstructed to accurately match their signature.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eUnrecognized Fields:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eImplementations \u003cstrong\u003eSHOULD\u003c/strong\u003e ignore unrecognized fields in messages, allowing for forward compatibility as the protocol evolves.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e5.8. Server Authentication Responsibilities\" href=\"#74-server-authentication-responsibilities\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe A2A Server:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eMUST\u003c/strong\u003e authenticate every incoming request based on the provided credentials and its declared authentication requirements.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSHOULD\u003c/strong\u003e use appropriate binding-specific error codes for authentication challenges or rejections.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSHOULD\u003c/strong\u003e provide relevant authentication challenge information with error responses.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e7.5. Server Authorization Responsibilities\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-75-server-authorization-responsibilities\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: 7.5. Server Authorization Responsibilities\" href=\"#75-server-authorization-responsibilities\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eOnce authenticated, the A2A Server authorizes requests based on the authenticated identity and its own policies. Authorization logic is implementation-specific and \u003cstrong\u003eMAY\u003c/strong\u003e consider:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eSpecific skills requested\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eActions attempted within tasks\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eData access policies\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eOAuth scopes (if applicable)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e7.6. In-Task Authorization\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-76-in-task-authorization\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: 7.6. In-Task Authorization\" href=\"#76-in-task-authorization\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eIn the course of performing a task, an agent may require authorization to perform some action. Examples include:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAn agent requiring an OAuth access token to call an API or another agent\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAn agent requiring human approval before a destructive action is taken\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eIn the sections below, we refer to the object that represents the approved authorization as a credential.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAgents may have multiple means for retrieving this authorization, such as via directly sending messages to a human.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eA2A provides the capability for agents to delegate the fulfillment of this authorization to the client via the \u003ccode\u003eTASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED\u003c/code\u003e Task state. This provides agents a fallback path for requesting authorization by passing the responsibility to the client.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch4 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e7.6.1 In-Task Authorization Agent Responsibilities\u003c/h4\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-761-in-task-authorization-agent-responsibilities\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: 7.6.1 In-Task Authorization Agent Responsibilities\" href=\"#761-in-task-authorization-agent-responsibilities\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eTo request that a client fulfills an authorization request, the agent:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eMUST use a Task to track the operation it is performing\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eMUST transition the TaskState to \u003ccode\u003eTASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eMUST include a TaskStatus message explaining the required authorization, unless the details of the authorization have been negotiated out-of-band or via an extension\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAgents MUST arrange to receive credentials via an out-of-band means, unless an in-band mechanism has been negotiated out-of-band or via an extension.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eIf the credential is received out-of-band, the agent SHOULD maintain any active response streams with the client after setting the TaskState to \u003ccode\u003eTASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED\u003c/code\u003e. The agent MAY immediately continue Task processing after receiving the credential, without a requirement that clients send a follow-up message.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAgents SHOULD support receiving messages directed to the Task while the Task remains in \u003ccode\u003eTASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED\u003c/code\u003e. This enables clients to negotiate, correct, or reject an authorization request.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch4 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e7.6.2 In-Task Authorization Client Responsibilities\u003c/h4\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-762-in-task-authorization-client-responsibilities\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: 7.6.2 In-Task Authorization Client Responsibilities\" href=\"#762-in-task-authorization-client-responsibilities\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0
