<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">3.3.3. Asynchronous Processing</h4><a id="user-content-333-asynchronous-processing" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 3.3.3. Asynchronous Processing" href="#333-asynchronous-processing"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">A2A operations are designed for asynchronous task execution. Operations return immediately with either <a href="#411-task"><code>Task</code></a> objects or <a href="#414-message"><code>Message</code></a> objects, and when a Task is returned, processing continues in the background. Clients retrieve task updates through polling, streaming, or push notifications (see <a href="#35-task-update-delivery-mechanisms">Section 3.5</a>). Agents MAY accept additional messages for tasks in non-terminal states to enable multi-turn interactions (see <a href="#34-multi-turn-interactions">Section 3.4</a>).</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">3.3.4. Capability Validation</h4><a id="user-content-334-capability-validation" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 3.3.4. Capability Validation" href="#334-capability-validation"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Agents declare optional capabilities in their <a href="#441-agentcard"><code>AgentCard</code></a>. When clients attempt to use operations or features that require capabilities not declared as supported in the Agent Card, the agent <strong>MUST</strong> return an appropriate error response:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Push Notifications</strong>: If <code>AgentCard.capabilities.pushNotifications</code> is <code>false</code> or not present, operations related to push notification configuration (Create, Get, List, Delete) <strong>MUST</strong> return <a href="#332-error-handling"><code>PushNotificationNotSupportedError</code></a>.</li>
<li><strong>Streaming</strong>: If <code>AgentCard.capabilities.streaming</code> is <code>false</code> or not present, attempts to use <code>SendStreamingMessage</code> or <code>SubscribeToTask</code> operations <strong>MUST</strong> return <a href="#332-error-handling"><code>UnsupportedOperationError</code></a>.</li>
<li><strong>Extended Agent Card</strong>: If <code>AgentCard.capabilities.extendedAgentCard</code> is <code>false</code> or not present, attempts to call the Get Extended Agent Card operation <strong>MUST</strong> return <a href="#332-error-handling"><code>UnsupportedOperationError</code></a>. If the agent declares support but has not configured an extended card, it <strong>MUST</strong> return <a href="#332-error-handling"><code>ExtendedAgentCardNotConfiguredError</code></a>.</li>
<li><strong>Extensions</strong>: When a server requests use of an extension marked as <code>required: true</code> in the Agent Card but the client does not declare support for it, the agent <strong>MUST</strong> return <a href="#332-error-handling"><code>ExtensionSupportRequiredError</code></a>.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Clients <strong>SHOULD</strong> validate capability support by examining the Agent Card before attempting operations that require optional capabilities.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">3.4. Multi-Turn Interactions</h3><a id="user-content-34-multi-turn-interactions" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 3.4. Multi-Turn Interactions" href="#34-multi-turn-interactions"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The A2A protocol supports multi-turn conversations through context identifiers and task references, enabling agents to maintain conversational continuity across multiple interactions.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">3.4.1. Context Identifier Semantics</h4><a id="user-content-341-context-identifier-semantics" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 3.4.1. Context Identifier Semantics" href="#341-context-identifier-semantics"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">A <code>contextId</code> is an identifier that logically groups multiple related <a href="#411-task"><code>Task</code></a> and <a href="#414-message"><code>Message</code></a> objects, providing continuity across a series of interactions.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Generation and Assignment:</strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Agents <strong>MAY</strong> generate a new <code>contextId</code> when processing a <a href="#414-message"><code>Message</code></a> that does not include a <code>contextId</code> field</li>
<li>If an agent generates a new <code>contextId</code>, it <strong>MUST</strong> be included in the response (either <a href="#411-task"><code>Task</code></a> or <a href="#414-message"><code>Message</code></a>)</li>
<li>Agents <strong>MAY</strong> accept and preserve client-provided <code>contextId</code> values</li>
<li>If an agent cannot accept a client-provided <code>contextId</code>, it <strong>MUST</strong> reject the request with an error and <strong>MUST NOT</strong> generate a new <code>contextId</code> for the response</li>
<li>Clients <strong>SHOULD NOT</strong> provide a client-generated <code>contextId</code> to a server unless they understand how the server will process that <code>contextId</code></li>
<li>Server-generated <code>contextId</code> values <strong>SHOULD</strong> be treated as opaque identifiers by clients</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Grouping and Scope:</strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>A <code>contextId</code> logically groups multiple <a href="#411-task"><code>Task</code></a> objects and <a href="#414-message"><code>Message</code></a> objects that are part of the same conversational context</li>
<li>All tasks and messages with the same <code>contextId</code> <strong>SHOULD</strong> be treated as part of the same conversational session</li>
<li>Agents <strong>MAY</strong> use the <code>contextId</code> to maintain internal state, conversational history, or LLM context across multiple interactions</li>
<li>Agents <strong>MAY</strong> implement context expiration or cleanup policies and <strong>SHOULD</strong> document any such policies</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">3.4.2. Task Identifier Semantics</h4><a id="user-content-342-task-identifier-semantics" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 3.4.2. Task Identifier Semantics" href="#342-task-identifier-semantics"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">A <code>taskId</code> is a unique identifier for a <a href="#411-task"><code>Task</code></a> object, representing a stateful unit of work with a defined lifecycle.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Generation and Assignment:</strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Task IDs are <strong>server-generated</strong> when a new task is created in response to a <a href="#414-message"><code>Message</code></a></li>
<li>Agents <strong>MUST</strong> generate a unique <code>taskId</code> for each new task they create</li>
<li>The generated <code>taskId</code> <strong>MUST</strong> be included in the <a href="#411-task"><code>Task</code></a> object returned to the client</li>
<li>When a client includes a <code>taskId</code> in a <a href="#414-message"><code>Message</code></a>, it <strong>MUST</strong> reference an existing task</li>
<li>Agents <strong>MUST</strong> return a <a href="#332-error-handling"><code>TaskNotFoundError</code></a> if the provided <code>taskId</code> does not correspond to an existing task</li>
<li>Client-provided <code>taskId</code> values for creating new tasks is <strong>NOT</strong> supported</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">3.4.3. Multi-Turn Conversation Patterns</h4><a id="user-content-343-multi-turn-conversation-patterns" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 3.4.3. Multi-Turn Conversation Patterns" href="#343-multi-turn-conversation-patterns"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The A2A protocol supports several patterns for multi-turn interactions:</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Context Continuity:</strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><a href="#411-task"><code>Task</code></a> objects maintain conversation context through the <code>contextId</code> field</li>
<li>Clients <strong>MAY</strong> include the <code>contextId</code> in subsequent messages to indicate continuation of a previous interaction</li>
<li>Clients <strong>MAY</strong> use <code>taskId</code> (with or without <code>contextId</code>) to continue or refine a specific task</li>
<li>Clients <strong>MAY</strong> use <code>contextId</code> without <code>taskId</code> to start a new task within an existing conversation context</li>
<li>Agents <strong>MUST</strong> infer <code>contextId</code> from the task if only <code>taskId</code> is provided</li>
<li>Agents <strong>MUST</strong> reject messages containing mismatching <code>contextId</code> and <code>taskId</code> (i.e., the provided <code>contextId</code> is different from that of the referenced <a href="#411-task"><code>Task</code></a>).</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Input Required State:</strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Agents can request additional input mid-processing by transitioning a task to the <code>input-required</code> state</li>
<li>The client continues the interaction by sending a new message with the same <code>taskId</code> and <code>contextId</code></li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Follow-up Messages:</strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Clients can send additional messages with <code>taskId</code> references to continue or refine existing tasks</li>
<li>Clients <strong>SHOULD</strong> use the <code>referenceTaskIds</code> field in <a href="#414-message"><code>Message</code></a> to explicitly reference related tasks</li>
<li>Agents <strong>SHOULD</strong> use referenced tasks to understand the context and intent of follow-up requests</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Context Inheritance:</strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>New tasks created within the same <code>contextId</code> can inherit context from previous interactions</li>
<li>Agents <strong>SHOULD</strong> leverage the shared <code>contextId</code> to provide contextually relevant responses</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">3.5. Task Update Delivery Mechanisms</h3><a id="user-content-35-task-update-delivery-mechanisms" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 3.5. Task Update Delivery Mechanisms" href="#35-task-update-delivery-mechanisms"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The A2A protocol provides three complementary mechanisms for clients to receive updates about task progress and completion.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">3.5.1. Overview of Update Mechanisms</h4><a id="user-content-351-overview-of-update-mechanisms" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 3.5.1. Overview of Update Mechanisms" href="#351-overview-of-update-mechanisms"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Polling (Get Task):</strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Client periodically calls Get Task (<a href="#313-get-task">Section 3.1.3</a>) to check task status</li>
<li>Simple to implement, works with all protocol bindings</li>
<li>Higher latency, potential for unnecessary requests</li>
<li>Best for: Simple integrations, infrequent updates, clients behind restrictive firewalls</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Streaming:</strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Real-time delivery of events as they occur</li>
<li>Operations: Send Streaming Message (<a href="#312-send-streaming-message">Section 3.1.2</a>) and Subscribe to Task (<a href="#316-subscribe-to-task">Section 3.1.6</a>)</li>
<li>Low latency, efficient for frequent updates</li>
<li>Requires persistent connection support</li>
<li>Best for: Interactive applications, real-time dashboards, live progress monitoring</li>
<li>Requires <code>AgentCard.capabilities.streaming</code> to be <code>true</code></li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Push Notifications (WebHooks):</strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Agent sends HTTP POST requests to client-registered endpoints when task state changes</li>
<li>Client does not maintain persistent connection</li>
<li>Asynchronous delivery, client must be reachable via HTTP</li>
<li>Best for: Server-to-server integrations, long-running tasks, event-driven architectures</li>
<li>Operations: Create (<a href="#317-create-push-notification-config">Section 3.1.7</a>), Get (<a href="#76-taskspushnotificationconfigget">Section 3.1.8</a>), List (<a href="#319-list-push-notification-configs">Section 3.1.9</a>), Delete (<a href="#3110-delete-push-notification-config">Section 3.1.10</a>)</li>
<li>Event types: TaskStatusUpdateEvent (<a href="#421-taskstatusupdateevent">Section 4.2.1</a>), TaskArtifactUpdateEvent (<a href="#422-taskartifactupdateevent">Section 4.2.2</a>), WebHook payloads (<a href="#43-push-notification-objects">Section 4.3</a>)</li>
<li>Requires <code>AgentCard.capabilities.pushNotifications</code> to be <code>true</code></li>
<li>Regardless of the protocol binding being used by the agent, WebHook calls use plain HTTP and the JSON payloads as defined in the HTTP protocol binding</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">3.5.2. Streaming Event Delivery</h4><a id="user-content-352-streaming-event-delivery" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 3.5.2. Streaming Event Delivery" href="#352-streaming-event-delivery"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Event Ordering:</strong></p>
<p dir="auto">All implementations MUST deliver events in the order they were generated. Events MUST NOT be reordered during transmission, regardless of protocol binding.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Multiple Streams Per Task:</strong></p>
<p dir="auto">An agent MAY serve multiple concurrent streams to one or more clients for the same task. This allows multiple clients (or the same client with multiple connections) to independently subscribe to and receive updates about a task's progress.</p>
<p dir="auto">When multiple streams are active for a task:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Events MUST be broadcast to all active streams for that task</li>
<li>Each stream MUST receive the same events in the same order</li>
<li>Closing one stream MUST NOT affect other active streams for the same task</li>
<li>The task lifecycle is independent of any individual stream's lifecycle</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">This capability enables scenarios such as:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Multiple team members monitoring the same long-running task</li>
<li>A client reconnecting to a task after a network interruption by opening a new stream</li>
<li>Different applications or dashboards displaying real-time updates for the same task</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">3.5.3. Push Notification Delivery</h4><a id="user-content-353-push-notification-delivery" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 3.5.3. Push Notification Delivery" href="#353-push-notification-delivery"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Push notifications are delivered via HTTP POST to client-registered webhook endpoints. The delivery semantics and reliability guarantees are defined in <a href="#43-push-notification-objects">Section 4.3</a>.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">3.6 Versioning</h3><a id="user-content-36-versioning" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 3.6 Versioning" href="#36-versioning"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The specific version of the A2A protocol in use is identified using the <code>Major.Minor</code> elements (e.g. <code>1.0</code>) of the corresponding A2A specification version. Patch version numbers used by the specification, do not affect protocol compatibility. Patch version numbers SHOULD NOT be used in requests, responses and Agent Cards, and MUST not be considered when clients and servers negotiate protocol versions.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">3.6.1 Client Responsibilities</h4><a id="user-content-361-client-responsibilities" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 3.6.1 Client Responsibilities" href="#361-client-responsibilities"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Clients MUST send the <code>A2A-Version</code> header with each request to maintain compatibility after an agent upgrades to a new version of the protocol (except for 0.3 Clients - 0.3 will be assumed for empty header). Sending the <code>A2A-Version</code> header also provides visibility to agents about version usage in the ecosystem, which can help inform the risks of inplace version upgrades.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Example of HTTP GET Request with Version Header:</strong></p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-httpspec notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto"><pre><span class="pl-k">GET</span><span class="pl-c1"> /tasks/task-123 HTTP/1.1</span>
<span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-v">Host:</span> agent.example.com</span>
<span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-v">A2A-Version:</span> 1.0</span>
<span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-v">Authorization:</span> Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...</span>
<span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-v">Accept:</span> application/json</span></pre><div class="zeroclipboard-container">

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">3.6.2 Server Responsibilities</h4><a id="user-content-362-server-responsibilities" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 3.6.2 Server Responsibilities" href="#362-server-responsibilities"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Agents MUST process requests using the semantics of the requested <code>A2A-Version</code> (matching <code>Major.Minor</code>). If the version is not supported by the interface, agents MUST return a <a href="#332-error-handling"><code>VersionNotSupportedError</code></a>.</p>
<p dir="auto">Agents MUST interpret empty value as 0.3 version.</p>
<p dir="auto">Agents CAN expose multiple interfaces for the same transport with different versions under the same or different URLs.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">3.6.3 Tooling support</h4><a id="user-content-363-tooling-support" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 3.6.3 Tooling support" href="#363-tooling-support"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Tooling libraries and SDKs that implement the A2A protocol MUST provide mechanisms to help clients manage protocol versioning, such as negotiation of the transport and protocol version used. Client Agents that require the latest features of the protocol should be configured to request specific versions and avoid automatic fallback to older versions, to prevent silently losing functionality.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">3.7 Messages and Artifacts</h3><a id="user-content-37-messages-and-artifacts" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 3.7 Messages and Artifacts" href="#37-messages-and-artifacts"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Messages and Artifacts serve distinct purposes within the A2A protocol. The core interaction model defined by A2A is for clients to send messages to initiate a task that produces one or more artifacts.</p>
<p dir="auto">Messages play several key roles:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Task Initiation</strong>: Clients send Messages to agents to initiate new tasks.</li>
<li><strong>Clarification Messages</strong>: Agents may send Messages back to the client to request clarification prior to initiating a task.</li>
<li><strong>Status Messages</strong>: Agents attach Messages to status update events to inform clients about task progress, request additional input, or provide informational updates.</li>
<li><strong>Task Interaction</strong>: Clients send Messages to provide additional input or instructions for ongoing tasks.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Messages SHOULD NOT be used to deliver task outputs. Results SHOULD BE returned using Artifacts associated with a Task. This separation allows for a clear distinction between communication (Messages) and data output (Artifacts).</p>
<p dir="auto">The Task History field contains Messages exchanged during task execution. However, not all Messages are guaranteed to be persisted in the Task history; for example, transient informational messages may not be stored. Messages exchanged prior to task creation may not be stored in Task history. The agent is responsible to determine which Messages are persisted in the Task History.</p>
<p dir="auto">Clients using streaming to retrieve task updates MAY not receive all status update messages if the client is disconnected and then reconnects. Messages MUST NOT be considered a reliable delivery mechanism for critical information.</p>
<p dir="auto">Agents MAY choose to persist all Messages that contain important information in the Task history to ensure clients can retrieve it later. However, clients MUST NOT rely on this behavior unless negotiated out-of-band.</p>

<p dir="auto">When a task update occurs, the agent sends an HTTP POST request to the configured webhook URL. The payload uses the same <a href="#323-stream-response"><code>StreamResponse</code></a> format as streaming operations, allowing push notifications to deliver the same event types as real-time streams.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Request Format:</strong></p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-httpspec notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto"><pre><span class="pl-k">POST</span> {<span class="pl-ii">webhook_url</span>}
<span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-v">Authorization:</span> {authentication_scheme} {credentials}</span>
<span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-v">Content-Type:</span> application/a2a+json</span>

{
  <span class="pl-ii">/* StreamResponse object - one of: */</span>
  <span class="pl-ent">"task"</span>: { <span class="pl-ii">/* Task object */ </span>},
  <span class="pl-ent">"message"</span>: { <span class="pl-ii">/* Message object */ </span>},
  <span class="pl-ent">"statusUpdate"</span>: { <span class="pl-ii">/* TaskStatusUpdateEvent object */ </span>},
  <span class="pl-ent">"artifactUpdate"</span>: { <span class="pl-ii">/* TaskArtifactUpdateEvent object */ </span>}
}</pre><div class="zeroclipboard-container">

}" tabindex="0" role="button">

<p dir="auto"><strong>Payload Structure:</strong></p>
<p dir="auto">The webhook payload is a <a href="#323-stream-response"><code>StreamResponse</code></a> object containing exactly one of the following:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>task</strong>: A <a href="#411-task"><code>Task</code></a> object with the current task state</li>
<li><strong>message</strong>: A <a href="#414-message"><code>Message</code></a> object containing a message response</li>
<li><strong>statusUpdate</strong>: A <a href="#421-taskstatusupdateevent"><code>TaskStatusUpdateEvent</code></a> indicating a status change</li>
<li><strong>artifactUpdate</strong>: A <a href="#422-taskartifactupdateevent"><code>TaskArtifactUpdateEvent</code></a> indicating artifact updates</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Authentication:</strong></p>
<p dir="auto">The agent MUST include authentication credentials in the request headers as specified in the <a href="#432-authenticationinfo"><code>PushNotificationConfig.authentication</code></a> field. The format follows standard HTTP authentication patterns (Bearer tokens, Basic auth, etc.).</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Client Responsibilities:</strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Clients MUST respond with HTTP 2xx status codes to acknowledge successful receipt</li>
<li>Clients SHOULD process notifications idempotently, as duplicate deliveries may occur</li>
<li>Clients MUST validate the task ID matches an expected task</li>
<li>Clients SHOULD implement appropriate security measures to verify the notification source</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Server Guarantees:</strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Agents MUST attempt delivery at least once for each configured webhook</li>
<li>Agents MAY implement retry logic with exponential backoff for failed deliveries</li>
<li>Agents SHOULD include a reasonable timeout for webhook requests (recommended: 10-30 seconds)</li>
<li>Agents MAY stop attempting delivery after a configured number of consecutive failures</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">For detailed security guidance on push notifications, see <a href="#132-push-notification-security">Section 13.2 Push Notification Security</a>.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">4.6. Extensions</h3><a id="user-content-46-extensions" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 4.6. Extensions" href="#46-extensions"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The A2A protocol supports extensions to provide additional functionality or data beyond the core specification while maintaining backward compatibility and interoperability. Extensions allow agents to declare additional capabilities such as protocol enhancements or vendor-specific features, maintain compatibility with clients that don't support specific extensions, enable innovation through experimental or domain-specific features without modifying the core protocol, and facilitate standardization by providing a pathway for community-developed features to become part of the core specification.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">4.6.1. Extension Declaration</h4><a id="user-content-461-extension-declaration" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 4.6.1. Extension Declaration" href="#461-extension-declaration"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Agents declare their supported extensions in the <a href="#441-agentcard"><code>AgentCard</code></a> using the <code>extensions</code> field, which contains an array of <a href="#444-agentextension"><code>AgentExtension</code></a> objects.</p>
<p dir="auto"><em>Example: Agent declaring extension support in AgentCard:</em></p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-json notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto"><pre>{
  <span class="pl-ent">"name"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>Research Assistant Agent<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
  <span class="pl-ent">"description"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>AI agent for academic research and fact-checking<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
  <span class="pl-ent">"supportedInterfaces"</span>: [
    {
      <span class="pl-ent">"url"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>https://research-agent.example.com/a2a/v1<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
      <span class="pl-ent">"protocolBinding"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>HTTP+JSON<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
      <span class="pl-ent">"protocolVersion"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>0.3<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
    }
  ],
  <span class="pl-ent">"capabilities"</span>: {
    <span class="pl-ent">"streaming"</span>: <span class="pl-c1">false</span>,
    <span class="pl-ent">"pushNotifications"</span>: <span class="pl-c1">false</span>,
    <span class="pl-ent">"extensions"</span>: [
      {
        <span class="pl-ent">"uri"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>https://standards.org/extensions/citations/v1<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
        <span class="pl-ent">"description"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>Provides citation formatting and source verification<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
        <span class="pl-ent">"required"</span>: <span class="pl-c1">false</span>
      },
      {
        <span class="pl-ent">"uri"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>https://example.com/extensions/geolocation/v1<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
        <span class="pl-ent">"description"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>Location-based search capabilities<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
        <span class="pl-ent">"required"</span>: <span class="pl-c1">false</span>
      }
    ]
  },
  <span class="pl-ent">"defaultInputModes"</span>: [<span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>text/plain<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>],
  <span class="pl-ent">"defaultOutputModes"</span>: [<span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>text/plain<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>],

<p dir="auto">Extensions can be integrated into the A2A protocol at several well-defined extension points:</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Message Extensions:</strong></p>
<p dir="auto">Messages can be extended to allow clients to provide additional strongly typed context or parameters relevant to the message being sent, or TaskStatus Messages to include extra information about the task's progress.</p>
<p dir="auto"><em>Example: A location extension using the extensions and metadata arrays:</em></p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-json notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto"><pre>{

      <span class="pl-ent">"longitude"</span>: <span class="pl-c1">-122.4194</span>,

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">4.6.3. Extension Versioning and Compatibility</h4><a id="user-content-463-extension-versioning-and-compatibility" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 4.6.3. Extension Versioning and Compatibility" href="#463-extension-versioning-and-compatibility"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Extensions <strong>SHOULD</strong> include version information in their URI identifier. This allows clients and agents to negotiate compatible versions of extensions during interactions. A new URI <strong>MUST</strong> be created for breaking changes to an extension.</p>
<p dir="auto">If a client requests a versions of an extension that the agent does not support, the agent <strong>SHOULD</strong> ignore the extension for that interaction and proceed without it, unless the extension is marked as <code>required</code> in the AgentCard, in which case the agent <strong>MUST</strong> return an error indicating unsupported extension. It <strong>MUST NOT</strong> fall back to a previous version of the extension automatically.</p>

<p dir="auto">When an agent supports multiple protocols, all supported protocols <strong>MUST</strong>:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Identical Functionality</strong>: Provide the same set of operations and capabilities</li>
<li><strong>Consistent Behavior</strong>: Return semantically equivalent results for the same requests</li>
<li><strong>Same Error Handling</strong>: Map errors consistently using appropriate protocol-specific codes</li>
<li><strong>Equivalent Authentication</strong>: Support the same authentication schemes declared in the AgentCard</li>
</ul>

JSON Field Naming Convention" href="#55-json-field-naming-convention"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">All JSON serializations of the A2A protocol data model <strong>MUST</strong> use <strong>camelCase</strong> naming for field names, not the snake_case convention used in Protocol Buffer definitions.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Naming Convention:</strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Protocol Buffer field: <code>protocol_version</code> → JSON field: <code>protocolVersion</code></li>
<li>Protocol Buffer field: <code>context_id</code> → JSON field: <code>contextId</code></li>
<li>Protocol Buffer field: <code>default_input_modes</code> → JSON field: <code>defaultInputModes</code></li>
<li>Protocol Buffer field: <code>push_notification_config</code> → JSON field: <code>pushNotificationConfig</code></li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Enum Values:</strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Enum values <strong>MUST</strong> be represented according to the <a href="https://protobuf.dev/programming-guides/json/" rel="nofollow">ProtoJSON specification</a>, which serializes enums as their string names <strong>as defined in the Protocol Buffer definition</strong> (typically SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE).</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Examples:</strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Protocol Buffer enum: <code>TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED</code> → JSON value: <code>"TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED"</code></li>
<li>Protocol Buffer enum: <code>ROLE_USER</code> → JSON value: <code>"ROLE_USER"</code></li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Note:</strong> This follows the ProtoJSON specification as adopted in <a href="/a2aproject/A2A/blob/main/adrs/adr-001-protojson-serialization.md">ADR-001</a>.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">5.6.1. Timestamps</h4><a id="user-content-561-timestamps" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 5.6.1. Timestamps" href="#561-timestamps"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The A2A protocol uses <a href="https://protobuf.dev/reference/protobuf/google.protobuf/#timestamp" rel="nofollow"><code>google.protobuf.Timestamp</code></a> for all timestamp fields in the Protocol Buffer definitions. When serialized to JSON (in JSON-RPC, HTTP/REST, or other JSON-based bindings), these timestamps <strong>MUST</strong> be represented as ISO 8601 formatted strings in UTC timezone.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Format Requirements:</strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Format:</strong> ISO 8601 combined date and time representation</li>
<li><strong>Timezone:</strong> UTC (denoted by 'Z' suffix)</li>
<li><strong>Precision:</strong> Millisecond precision <strong>SHOULD</strong> be used where available</li>
<li><strong>Pattern:</strong> <code>YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ</code></li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Examples:</strong></p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-json notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto"><pre>{
  <span class="pl-ent">"timestamp"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>2025-10-28T10:30:00.000Z<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
  <span class="pl-ent">"createdAt"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>2025-10-28T14:25:33.142Z<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
  <span class="pl-ent">"lastModified"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>2025-10-31T17:45:22.891Z<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>
}</pre><div class="zeroclipboard-container">

<p dir="auto"><strong>Implementation Notes:</strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Protocol Buffer's <code>google.protobuf.Timestamp</code> represents time as seconds since Unix epoch (January 1, 1970, 00:00:00 UTC) plus nanoseconds</li>
<li>JSON serialization automatically converts this to ISO 8601 format when using standard Protocol Buffer JSON encoding</li>
<li>Clients and servers <strong>MUST</strong> parse and generate ISO 8601 timestamps correctly</li>
<li>When millisecond precision is not available, the fractional seconds portion <strong>MAY</strong> be omitted or zero-filled</li>
<li>Timestamps <strong>MUST NOT</strong> include timezone offsets other than 'Z' (all times are UTC)</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">5.7. Field Presence and Optionality</h3><a id="user-content-57-field-presence-and-optionality" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 5.7. Field Presence and Optionality" href="#57-field-presence-and-optionality"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The Protocol Buffer definition in <code>specification/a2a.proto</code> uses <a href="https://github.com/googleapis/googleapis/blob/master/google/api/field_behavior.proto"><code>google.api.field_behavior</code></a> annotations to indicate whether fields are <code>REQUIRED</code>. These annotations serve as both documentation and validation hints for implementations.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Required Fields:</strong></p>
<p dir="auto">Fields marked with <code>[(google.api.field_behavior) = REQUIRED]</code> indicate that the field <strong>MUST</strong> be present and set in valid messages. Implementations <strong>SHOULD</strong> validate these requirements and reject messages with missing required fields. Arrays marked as required <strong>MUST</strong> contain at least one element.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Optional Field Presence:</strong></p>
<p dir="auto">The Protocol Buffer <code>optional</code> keyword is used to distinguish between a field being explicitly set versus omitted. This distinction is critical for two scenarios:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Explicit Default Values:</strong> Some fields in the specification define default values that differ from Protocol Buffer's implicit defaults. Implementations should apply the default value when the field is not explicitly provided.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Agent Card Canonicalization:</strong> When creating cryptographic signatures of Agent Cards, it is required to produce a canonical JSON representation. The <code>optional</code> keyword enables implementations to distinguish between fields that were explicitly set (and should be included in the canonical form) versus fields that were omitted (and should be excluded from canonicalization). This ensures Agent Cards can be reconstructed to accurately match their signature.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Unrecognized Fields:</strong></p>
<p dir="auto">Implementations <strong>SHOULD</strong> ignore unrecognized fields in messages, allowing for forward compatibility as the protocol evolves.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">5.8. Custom Binding Identification</h3><a id="user-content-58-custom-binding-identification" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 5.8. Custom Binding Identification" href="#58-custom-binding-identification"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Custom protocol bindings <strong>SHOULD</strong> be identified by a URI. Using a URI as the
identifier provides globally unique identification across all implementers.</p>
<p dir="auto">The <code>protocolBinding</code> field in the Agent Card's <code>supportedInterfaces</code> entry
<strong>SHOULD</strong> be a URI:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-json notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto"><pre>{
  <span class="pl-ent">"supportedInterfaces"</span>: [
    {
      <span class="pl-ent">"url"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>wss://agent.example.com/a2a/websocket<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
      <span class="pl-ent">"protocolBinding"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>https://example.com/bindings/websocket/v1<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
      <span class="pl-ent">"protocolVersion"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>1.0<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>
    }
  ]
}</pre><div class="zeroclipboard-container">

<p dir="auto"><strong>Scenario:</strong> Client requests a long-running report generation and wants to be notified via webhook when it's done.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Initial Request with Push Notification Config:</strong></p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-httpspec notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto"><pre><span class="pl-k">POST</span><span class="pl-c1"> /message:send HTTP/1.1</span>
<span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-v">Host:</span> agent.example.com</span>
<span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-v">Content-Type:</span> application/a2a+json</span>
<span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-v">Authorization:</span> Bearer token</span>

{
  <span class="pl-ent">"message"</span>: {
    <span class="pl-ent">"role"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>ROLE_USER<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
    <span class="pl-ent">"parts"</span>: [
      {
        <span class="pl-ent">"text"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>Generate the Q1 sales report. This usually takes a while. Notify me when it's ready.<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>
      }
    ],
    <span class="pl-ent">"messageId"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>6dbc13b5-bd57-4c2b-b503-24e381b6c8d6<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>
  },
  <span class="pl-ent">"configuration"</span>: {
    <span class="pl-ent">"taskPushNotificationConfig"</span>: {
      <span class="pl-ent">"url"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>https://client.example.com/webhook/a2a-notifications<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
      <span class="pl-ent">"authentication"</span>: {
        <span class="pl-ent">"scheme"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>Bearer<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
        <span class="pl-ent">"credentials"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>secure-client-token-for-task-aaa<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>
      }
    }
  }
}</pre><div class="zeroclipboard-container">

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">7. Authentication and Authorization</h2><a id="user-content-7-authentication-and-authorization" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 7. Authentication and Authorization" href="#7-authentication-and-authorization"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">A2A treats agents as standard enterprise applications, relying on established web security practices. Identity information is handled at the protocol layer, not within A2A semantics.</p>
<p dir="auto">For a comprehensive guide on enterprise security aspects, see <a href="/a2aproject/A2A/blob/main/docs/topics/enterprise-ready.md">Enterprise-Ready Features</a>.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">7.1. Protocol Security</h3><a id="user-content-71-protocol-security" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 7.1. Protocol Security" href="#71-protocol-security"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Production deployments <strong>MUST</strong> use encrypted communication (HTTPS for HTTP-based bindings, TLS for gRPC). Implementations <strong>SHOULD</strong> use modern TLS configurations (TLS 1.3+ recommended) with strong cipher suites.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">7.2. Server Identity Verification</h3><a id="user-content-72-server-identity-verification" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 7.2. Server Identity Verification" href="#72-server-identity-verification"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">A2A Clients <strong>SHOULD</strong> verify the A2A Server's identity by validating its TLS certificate against trusted certificate authorities (CAs) during the TLS handshake.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">7.3. Client Authentication Process</h3><a id="user-content-73-client-authentication-process" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 7.3. Client Authentication Process" href="#73-client-authentication-process"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ol dir="auto">
<li><strong>Discovery of Requirements:</strong> The client discovers the server's required authentication schemes via the <code>securitySchemes</code> field in the AgentCard.</li>
<li><strong>Credential Acquisition (Out-of-Band):</strong> The client obtains the necessary credentials through an out-of-band process specific to the required authentication scheme.</li>
<li><strong>Credential Transmission:</strong> The client includes these credentials in protocol-appropriate headers or metadata for every A2A request.</li>
</ol>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">7.4. Server Authentication Responsibilities</h3><a id="user-content-74-server-authentication-responsibilities" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 7.4. Server Authentication Responsibilities" href="#74-server-authentication-responsibilities"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The A2A Server:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>MUST</strong> authenticate every incoming request based on the provided credentials and its declared authentication requirements.</li>
<li><strong>SHOULD</strong> use appropriate binding-specific error codes for authentication challenges or rejections.</li>
<li><strong>SHOULD</strong> provide relevant authentication challenge information with error responses.</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">7.5. Server Authorization Responsibilities</h3><a id="user-content-75-server-authorization-responsibilities" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 7.5. <p dir="auto">Once authenticated, the A2A Server authorizes requests based on the authenticated identity and its own policies. Authorization logic is implementation-specific and <strong>MAY</strong> consider:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Specific skills requested</li>
<li>Actions attempted within tasks</li>
<li>Data access policies</li>
<li>OAuth scopes (if applicable)</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">7.6. In-Task Authorization</h3><a id="user-content-76-in-task-authorization" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 7.6. In-Task Authorization" href="#76-in-task-authorization"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">In the course of performing a task, an agent may require authorization to perform some action. Examples include:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>An agent requiring an OAuth access token to call an API or another agent</li>
<li>An agent requiring human approval before a destructive action is taken</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">In the sections below, we refer to the object that represents the approved authorization as a credential.</p>
<p dir="auto">Agents may have multiple means for retrieving this authorization, such as via directly sending messages to a human.</p>
<p dir="auto">A2A provides the capability for agents to delegate the fulfillment of this authorization to the client via the <code>TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED</code> Task state. This provides agents a fallback path for requesting authorization by passing the responsibility to the client.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">7.6.1 In-Task Authorization Agent Responsibilities</h4><a id="user-content-761-in-task-authorization-agent-responsibilities" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 7.6.1 In-Task Authorization Agent Responsibilities" href="#761-in-task-authorization-agent-responsibilities"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">To request that a client fulfills an authorization request, the agent:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>MUST use a Task to track the operation it is performing</li>
<li>MUST transition the TaskState to <code>TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED</code></li>
<li>MUST include a TaskStatus message explaining the required authorization, unless the details of the authorization have been negotiated out-of-band or via an extension</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">Agents MUST arrange to receive credentials via an out-of-band means, unless an in-band mechanism has been negotiated out-of-band or via an extension.</p>
<p dir="auto">If the credential is received out-of-band, the agent SHOULD maintain any active response streams with the client after setting the TaskState to <code>TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED</code>. The agent MAY immediately continue Task processing after receiving the credential, without a requirement that clients send a follow-up message.</p>
<p dir="auto">Agents SHOULD support receiving messages directed to the Task while the Task remains in <code>TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED</code>. This enables clients to negotiate, correct, or reject an authorization request.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">7.6.2 In-Task Authorization Client Responsibilities</h4><a id="user-content-762-in-task-authorization-client-responsibilities" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 7.6.2 In-Task Authorization Client Responsibilities" href="#762-in-task-authorization-client-responsibilities"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Upon receiving a Task in <code>TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED</code>, a client is expected to take action in some way to resolve the agent's request for authorization.</p>
<p dir="auto">A client may:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Send a response message to the Task to negotiate, correct, or reject the authorization request.</li>
<li>Contact another human, agent, or service to fulfill the authorization request</li>
<li>Directly fulfill the authorization request via an out-of-band or extension negotiated means</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">If the client is itself an A2A agent actively processing a Task, the client may further delegate the authorization request to its client by transitioning its own Task to <code>TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED</code>. The client SHOULD follow all <a href="#761-in-task-authorization-agent-responsibilities">In-Task Authorization Agent Responsibilities</a>. This enables forming a chain of Tasks in <code>TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED</code>.</p>
<p dir="auto">Clients may not be aware of when the agent receives credentials out-of-band and subsequently continues Task processing. If a client does not have an active response stream open with the agent, the client risks missing Task updates. To avoid this, a client SHOULD perform one of the following:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Subscribe to a stream of events for the Task using the <a href="#316-subscribe-to-task">Subscribe to Task</a> operation</li>
<li>Register a webhook to receive events, if supported by the agent, using the <a href="#317-create-push-notification-config">Create Push Notification Config</a> operation</li>
<li>Begin polling the Task using the <a href="#313-get-task">Get Task</a> operation</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">7.6.3 In-Task Authorization Security Considerations</h4><a id="user-content-763-in-task-authorization-security-considerations" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 7.6.3 In-Task Authorization Security Considerations" href="#763-in-task-authorization-security-considerations"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Agents SHOULD receive credentials for in-task authorization requests out of band via a secure channel, such as HTTPS. This ensures that credentials are provided directly to the agent.</p>
<p dir="auto">In-band credential exchange may be negotiated via out-of-band means or by using extensions. In-band credential exchange can allow credentials to be passed across chains of multiple A2A agents, exposing those credentials to each agent participating in the chain.</p>
<p dir="auto">If using in-band credential exchange, we recommend adhering to the following security practices:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Credentials SHOULD be bound to the agent which originated the request, such that only this agent is able to use the credentials. This ensures that credentials propagating through a chain of A2A requests are only usable by the requesting agent.</li>
<li>Credentials containing sensitive information SHOULD be only readable by the agent which originated the request, such as by encrypting the credential.</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">7.6.4 In-Task Authorization Scope</h4><a id="user-content-764-in-task-authorization-scope" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 7.6.4 In-Task Authorization Scope" href="#764-in-task-authorization-scope"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The <code>TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED</code> state signals that additional authorization is required to continue processing a Task. The A2A protocol does not define the scope, representation, validity, or revocation semantics of the authorization decision or credential obtained in response to this state.</p>
<p dir="auto">Agents MUST NOT treat the <code>TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED</code> state transition, by itself, as authorization for any particular operation. The meaning and scope of any resulting authorization decision or credential MUST be defined by the agent's implementation, by the credential issuer, or by an A2A extension.</p>
<p dir="auto">If an implementation requires authorization for specific operations, it is responsible for defining how the authorized operation is identified and how that authorization is checked before the operation is performed.</p>
<p dir="auto">A credential or authorization decision obtained while a Task is in <code>TASK_STATE_AUTH_REQUIRED</code> MUST NOT be assumed to authorize subsequent messages on the Task unless that behavior is explicitly defined by the implementation, credential issuer, or extension.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">8. Agent Discovery: The Agent Card</h2><a id="user-content-8-agent-discovery-the-agent-card" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 8. Agent Discovery: The Agent Card" href="#8-agent-discovery-the-agent-card"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
