<p dir="auto"><strong>Encoding considerations:</strong> Binary (UTF-8 encoding MUST be used for JSON text)</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Security considerations:</strong>
This media type shares security considerations common to all JSON-based formats as described in RFC 8259, Section 12. Additionally:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Content MUST be validated against the A2A protocol schema before processing</li>
<li>Implementations MUST sanitize user-provided content to prevent injection attacks</li>
<li>File references within A2A messages MUST be validated to prevent server-side request forgery (SSRF)</li>
<li>Authentication and authorization MUST be enforced as specified in Section 7 of the A2A specification</li>
<li>Sensitive information in task history and artifacts MUST be protected according to applicable data protection regulations</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Interoperability considerations:</strong>
The A2A protocol supports multiple protocol bindings. This media type is intended for the HTTP+JSON/REST binding.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Published specification:</strong>
Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol Specification, available at: <a href="https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification" rel="nofollow">https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification</a></p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Applications that use this media type:</strong>

<p dir="auto"><strong>URI suffix:</strong> agent-card.json</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Change controller:</strong> A2A Protocol Working Group</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Specification document:</strong> Section 8.2 of the A2A Protocol Specification</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Related information:</strong>
The <code>.well-known/agent-card.json</code> URI provides a standardized location for discovering an A2A agent's capabilities, supported protocols, authentication requirements, and available skills. The resource at this URI MUST return an AgentCard object as defined in Section 4.4.1 of the A2A specification.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Status:</strong> Permanent</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Security considerations:</strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>The Agent Card MAY contain public information about an agent's capabilities and SHOULD NOT include sensitive credentials or internal implementation details</li>
<li>Implementations SHOULD support HTTPS to ensure authenticity and integrity of the Agent Card</li>
<li>Agent Cards MAY be signed using JSON Web Signatures (JWS) as specified in the AgentCardSignature object (Section 4.4.7)</li>
<li>Clients SHOULD verify signatures when present to ensure the Agent Card has not been tampered with</li>
<li>Extended Agent Cards retrieved via authenticated endpoints (Section 3.1.11) MAY contain additional information and MUST enforce appropriate access controls</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Example:</strong></p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto"><pre lang="text" class="notranslate"><code>https://agent.example.com/.well-known/agent-card.json

<p dir="auto"><strong>Affected Types:</strong></p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Part Union Types</strong>:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>TextPart</strong>:
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Legacy:</strong> <code>{ "kind": "text", "text": "..." }</code></li>
<li><strong>Current:</strong> <code>{ "text": "..." }</code> (member presence acts as discriminator)</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>FilePart</strong>:
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Legacy:</strong> <code>{ "kind": "file", "file": { "name": "...", "mimeType": "...", "fileWithBytes": "..." } }</code></li>
<li><strong>Current:</strong> <code>{ "raw": "...", "filename": "...", "mediaType": "..." }</code> (or <code>url</code> instead of <code>raw</code>)</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>DataPart</strong>:
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Legacy:</strong> <code>{ "kind": "data", "data": {...} }</code></li>
<li><strong>Current:</strong> <code>{ "data": {...}, "mediaType": "application/json" }</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Streaming Event Types</strong>:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>TaskStatusUpdateEvent</strong>:
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Legacy:</strong> <code>{ "kind": "status-update", "taskId": "...", "status": {...} }</code></li>
<li><strong>Current:</strong> <code>{ "statusUpdate": { "taskId": "...", "status": {...} } }</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>TaskArtifactUpdateEvent</strong>:
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Legacy:</strong> <code>{ "kind": "artifact-update", "taskId": "...", "artifact": {...} }</code></li>
<li><strong>Current:</strong> <code>{ "artifactUpdate": { "taskId": "...", "artifact": {...} } }</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Migration Strategy:</strong></p>
<p dir="auto">For <strong>Clients</strong> upgrading from pre-0.3.x:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>Update parsers to expect wrapper objects with member names as discriminators</li>
<li>When constructing requests, use the new wrapper format</li>
<li>Implement version detection based on the agent's <code>protocolVersions</code> in the <code>AgentCard</code></li>
<li>Consider maintaining backward compatibility by detecting and handling both formats during a transition period</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">For <strong>Servers</strong> upgrading from pre-0.3.x:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>Update serialization logic to emit wrapper objects</li>
<li><strong>Breaking:</strong> The <code>kind</code> field is no longer part of the protocol and should not be emitted</li>
<li>Update deserialization to expect wrapper objects with member names</li>
<li>Ensure the <code>AgentCard</code> declares the correct <code>protocolVersions</code> (e.g., ["1.0"] or later)</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Rationale:</strong></p>
<p dir="auto">This change aligns with modern API design practices and Protocol Buffers' <code>oneof</code> semantics, where the field name itself serves as the type discriminator. This approach:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Reduces redundancy (no need for both a field name and a <code>kind</code> value)</li>
<li>Aligns JSON-RPC and gRPC representations more closely</li>
<li>Simplifies code generation from schema definitions</li>
<li>Eliminates the need for representing inheritance structures in schema languages</li>
<li>Improves type safety in strongly-typed languages</li>
</ul>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Appendix B. Relationship to MCP (Model Context Protocol)</h2><a id="user-content-appendix-b-relationship-to-mcp-model-context-protocol" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Appendix B. Relationship to MCP (Model Context Protocol)" href="#appendix-b-relationship-to-mcp-model-context-protocol"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">A2A and MCP are complementary protocols designed for different aspects of agentic systems:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong><a href="https://modelcontextprotocol.io/" rel="nofollow">Model Context Protocol (MCP)</a>:</strong> Focuses on standardizing how AI models and agents connect to and interact with <strong>tools, APIs, data sources, and other external resources.</strong> It defines structured ways to describe tool capabilities (like function calling in LLMs), pass inputs, and receive structured outputs. Think of MCP as the "how-to" for an agent to <em>use</em> a specific capability or access a resource.</li>
<li><strong>Agent2Agent Protocol (A2A):</strong> Focuses on standardizing how independent, often opaque, <strong>AI agents communicate and collaborate with each other as peers.</strong> A2A provides an application-level protocol for agents to discover each other, negotiate interaction modalities, manage shared tasks, and exchange conversational context or complex results. It's about how agents <em>partner</em> or <em>delegate</em> work.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto"><strong>How they work together:</strong>
An A2A Client agent might request an A2A Server agent to perform a complex task. The Server agent, in turn, might use MCP to interact with several underlying tools, APIs, or data sources to gather information or perform actions necessary to fulfill the A2A task.</p>
<p dir="auto">For a more detailed comparison, see the <a href="/a2aproject/A2A/blob/main/docs/topics/a2a-and-mcp.md">A2A and MCP guide</a>.</p>
